source: a 3D third-person collectathon adventure: you explore an open 3D world with the default Roblox character, run and jump across ground and raised platforms, collect coins/gems scattered around the level, and reach a goal once you've gathered enough. Use the built-in Roblox character movement and camera (WASD to move, Space to jump). Track collected coins on a HUD and show a clear win when the goal is reached, and respawn the player if they fall off the world. DO NOT ASK ANY QUESTIONS JUST COMPLETE

image_prompt.text: Raised platforms and stepped ledges over the ground, spaced for running long jumps between them
Tucked-away pockets rewarding players who leave the obvious route
A barrier in front of the goal that stays shut until enough coins and gems are collected
A board in the world showing the collectible total still outstanding
A distinct goal area at the end of the world, visibly the payoff

layout_placement.text: Coins and gems scattered across the ground and on the raised platforms
Return points the player respawns to instead of restarting, including after falling off the world
The goal trigger that fires the win once the player reaches it with enough collected
Tracker bound to the collected count so the goal gate knows when to open

notes: Close dominance call: the sentence is about a collectathon adventure, so Adventure owns the shape and preset and Obby contributes the platform options only.

Obby declares a genre-wide P6 route for physics-legal jump spacing, but that code lives on its shape rows; under an open-world shape this emits P0 and the jump spacing goes unvalidated. Worth flagging to the generator.
Checkpoint deduped to the Adventure wording, which is a placed save point; the Obby version also draws a landing pad, and that visible half is lost by the dedupe rule.
The HUD coin counter and win screen are screen-space and have no stream here.

open_questions.ask: No visual style was given - should the world be stylized and colourful, or naturalistic? (The prompt asked not to be asked, so a neutral dressing is being used.)
How many coins or gems count as enough to open the goal?

answers.ask: No visual style was given - should the world be stylized and colourful, or naturalistic? (The prompt asked not to be asked, so a neutral dressing is being used.)
answers.answer: Use a stylized, colourful Roblox-style world; keep the dressing simple and readable for platforming.

answers.ask: How many coins or gems count as enough to open the goal?
answers.answer: Require 10 collected coins or gems to open the goal, keeping the level a small, plainly playable vertical slice.
